cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: I'm very pleased to welcome this evening's guest speaker, Mark Logan, who's going to tell

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: us about the recent transformation of Minster Park. Over to you, Mark.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Thank you. I'm sure you're all familiar with Minster Park.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: It's been a feature of the city for well over a century, and has been the responsibility

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: of the city council for most of that time.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: What perhaps isn't so well known is the origin of the park: unlike many public parks that

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: started in private ownership, as the garden of a large house, for instance, Minster was

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: some waste land, which people living nearby started planting with flowers in 1892.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: It was unclear who actually owned the land, and this wasn't settled until 20 years later,

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: when the council took possession of it.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: You may have noticed the statue near one of the entrances.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: It's of Diane Gosforth, who played a key role in the history of the park.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Once the council had become the legal owner, it planned to sell the land for housing.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Many local people wanted it to remain a place that everyone could go to, to enjoy the

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: fresh air and natural environment – remember the park is in a densely populated

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: residential area.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Diane Gosforth was one of those people, and she organised petitions and demonstrations,

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: which eventually made the council change its mind about the future of the land.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Soon after this the First World War broke out, in 1914, and most of the park was dug up

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: and planted with vegetables, which were sold locally.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: At one stage the army considered taking in over for troop exercises and got as far as

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: contacting the city council, then decided the park was too small to be of use.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: There were occasional public meetings during the war, in an area that had been retained

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: as grass.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: After the war, the park was turned back more or less to how it had been before 1914, and

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: continued almost unchanged until recently.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: Plans for transforming it were drawn up at various times, most recently in 2013, though

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: they were revised in 2015, before any work had started.

cues.speaker: AN
cues.text: The changes finally got going in 2016, and were finished on schedule last year.
